title: PPT-assisted capacities of bosonic Gaussian channels
abstract: We determine the exact quantum communication and entanglement-distribution capacities of three fundamental bosonic channels, namely thermal loss, thermal amplification and additive Gaussian noise, assisted by operations that completely preserve positive partial transpose (PPT). These operations are more powerful than local operations and classical communication (LOCC), but cannot generate distillable entanglement on their own. For thermal loss, the unconstrained capacity coincides with the Pirandola-Laurenza-Ottaviani-Banchi (PLOB) bound throughout the non-entanglement-breaking regime. The corresponding upper bounds are also attained for thermal amplification and additive noise. We extend these results to energy-constrained communication, establishing exact capacities for all three channels at every prescribed mean input energy. Our results solve a class of bosonic capacity problems under PPT assistance and establish exact benchmarks for determining whether the same communication rates can be achieved via LOCC alone.
summary: This paper calculates the exact quantum communication and entanglement-distribution capacities for key bosonic Gaussian channels (loss, amplification, noise) under the assistance of PPT-preserving operations. It establishes that these capacities match known theoretical bounds across both unconstrained and energy-constrained settings. The results provide crucial benchmarks for understanding the limits of quantum information transmission through noisy optical and microwave channels.
main_problem: The paper determines the exact quantum communication and entanglement-distribution capacities of three fundamental bosonic Gaussian channels (thermal loss, amplification, and additive noise) when assisted by PPT-preserving operations.
main_result: The PPT-assisted capacity for all three channels is found to coincide with the established PLOB bound, and these exact capacities are derived for both unconstrained and energy-constrained regimes.
method: The analysis uses techniques involving collective distillation maps, establishing lower and upper bounds by matching constructive protocols with converse arguments.
model_or_system: The system involves bosonic Gaussian channels, modeling physical processes like optical attenuation (thermal loss), amplification, and Gaussian noise, characterized by parameters like transmissivity ($\eta$), mean photon numbers ($n, \xi$), and energy constraints ($N$).
key_observables: Quantum capacity ($	ext{QPPT}$), Entanglement-distribution capacity ($	ext{DPPT}$), and the PLOB bound.
important_parameters: Transmissivity ($\eta$), environment mean photon number ($n$), amplifier gain ($\kappa$), added mean photon number ($\xi$), and the energy constraint $N$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the power of PPT-preserving operations, which are shown to be more powerful than LOCC but less powerful than unrestricted operations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the capacity for each channel (loss, amplification, noise) first in the unconstrained setting, establishing equality with known bounds, and then extends the results to the energy-constrained regime using functional forms $F(N)$.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, exact capacity formulas for fundamental noise channels relevant to quantum communication, directly impacting the theoretical limits of quantum networking and quantum sensing.
